clue.text: First fop prepared to go naked?

indicators.note: the letters are made ready in a new order, so prepared signals rearranging the two words before it

explanation.surface: A dandy gets himself ready to take his clothes off for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' tells you to rearrange the letters of FIRST FOP.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip off is to remove all one's clothes, an idiom for undressing completely.

clue.text: Artificial channel cut across middle of obstruction

indicators.note: spanning, so the word for cut is placed round the central letter

parts.note: to slice is to cut

indicators.note: the central letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A man-made channel is cut right through the middle of a blockage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' picks U, the central letter of OBSTRUCTION, and 'across' puts SLICE round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluice is a man-made water channel controlled by a gate.

clue.text: British leaving to make way across watershed.

indicators.note: going away, so the letter for British is removed

parts.note: to bridge something is to make a way across it

explanation.surface: The British pull out after building a route over a dividing ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIDGE, the verb for spanning a gap, loses its B ('British leaving').
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of high ground divides river systems, which is what a watershed is in geography.

clue.text: … experience range with almost unlimited vista

indicators.note: nearly all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: pure means absolute or unqualified, as in pure chance
a vista is a view

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the walker takes in a far-reaching panorama from the ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PURE to PUR. The ellipsis only links the surface to 2 Down; 'experience range' is read together as the definition, purview being the range of one's experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Purview is the scope or extent of one's experience or authority, so a range of experience.

clue.text: What's great about obese woman chasing achievement as a boxer

indicators.note: following behind, so this piece comes after the word for achievement

parts.note: a feat is a notable achievement
a fat woman's notable feature is her weight, split as the two words her and weight

explanation.surface: An overweight woman is described chasing success as a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' puts HER WEIGHT after FEAT; the cheeky phrase reads 'what is great' about a fat woman as her weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A featherweight is a boxer in a light weight division, so one kind of boxer.

clue.text: Advise what Pam needs to take for pain

wordplay.reading: PAM to PAIN: two letters replace one

parts.words: what Pam needs to take for pain
parts.note: a letter puzzle: to turn the name Pam into the word pain, two letters must be taken in place of its last letter, and stating that swap in three short words gives the entry

explanation.surface: A friend called Pam is told which tablet to swallow for her aches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take for pain' suggests a painkiller, but it is a letter swap: PAM becomes PAIN by taking IN in place of M, and the swap itself, IN FOR M, run together gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To advise someone is to tell or notify them, a synonym in the sense of giving information.

clue.text: Tell managed to get up speed

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the word backwards

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get moving faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' reverses RAN to NAR, since in a down clue going up means reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell a story; both verbs mean recount.

clue.text: Where boundaries must have been crossed if film's to get broadcast

definitions.text: Where boundaries must have been crossed

indicators.note: spread about widely, so the letters before it are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Censors draw lines a film must not overstep if it is to be shown on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get broadcast' tells you to rearrange IF FILMS TO, keeping the S of film's.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-limits place is out of bounds, so going there means crossing a boundary.

clue.text: Tons keep quiet when entering into extra borrowing arrangement

indicators.note: going inside, so these pieces sit within the word for extra

parts.note: more means extra or additional
to gag someone is to keep them quiet

explanation.surface: Tons of money are kept quiet when people take on more debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering into' puts T and GAG inside MORE; 'Tons' is the abbreviation T, not money, despite the borrowing surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortgage is a loan secured on property, a standard borrowing arrangement.

clue.text: Way of bowling done deviously through cover

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a delivery with the hand below the shoulder
read as two words, beneath a hand, i.e. kept covered

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the cricket style of bowling with the arm below shoulder height, the adjective for sly dealing, and the literal phrase 'under hand', meaning concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Underarm cricket bowling, sly conduct, and something hidden beneath a hand all share this single word.

clue.text: What's made only to snap in bits?

definitions.text: What's made only to snap in bits?

parts.words: What's made only to snap in bits?
parts.note: sounds like something built to break into pieces, but snap means take a photograph and bits are the binary digits it records in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap' suggests breaking and 'bits' suggests fragments; in fact it is taking pictures and computer bits.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera that records snapshots as binary data in bits rather than on film is the digital kind.

clue.text: Send to specialist, concerned with iron reading barely showing

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: only a bare minimum of the word is visible, so just its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A doctor checks an iron level reading that barely registers and sends the patient on to a consultant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely showing' keeps only the first letter of 'reading'. The medical surface makes 'iron reading' look like a blood test.
explanation.definitionFit: A GP who refers a patient passes them on to a consultant, the standard medical usage.

clue.text: Church father's returning hot treasure

indicators.note: coming back means the word for father is read backwards

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A priest comes back to the church to find a valuable hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses SIRE to ERIS; 'treasure' is a verb here, not a noun as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish something is to treasure it, holding it dear; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Confining to school involves Rugby's head being harsh

indicators.note: takes in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: gating is the British school punishment of keeping a pupil within the grounds

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A headmaster at Rugby, an English public school, harshly confines pupils to the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' puts R (the first letter of Rugby, signalled by 'head') inside GATING. Rugby is a famous English boarding school, so 'head' looks like its headmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating noise is rasping and harsh, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Prestige owner arranged for help in driving

indicators.note: set out in a different order, signalling that the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who owns a prestige car has it set up to make driving easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' tells you to rearrange the letters of PRESTIGE OWNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Power steering is a car system that assists the driver in turning the wheels.

clue.text: Sponsorship scrapped for pageant that lacks following

indicators.note: broken up, so the letters of these words are mixed into a new order

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: The sponsorship for a pageant is cancelled when it fails to attract supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrapped' signals the anagram, and 'that lacks following' removes F, so FOR PAGEANT less F is rearranged; F for following is a common reference abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Patronage is the support given by a patron, essentially sponsorship.

clue.text: Tom perhaps asked what's new in cinema?

definitions.meaning: a tom is a male cat, a pet example
What's New ...? is a 1965 film comedy, whose title is a question

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' is a male cat, and the second part refers to the 1965 film 'What's New Pussycat?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomcat is an example of a cat, and the film title addresses one by its pet name.

clue.text: We pot blue — shot's complicated and very involved

indicators.note: made tangled or intricate, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A snooker player trying to pot the blue ball faces a tricky shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' tells you to rearrange WE POT BLUE SHOT; the 's is read as 'is', not as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up to the elbows in something is an idiom for being deeply busy with or engaged in it.

clue.text: Perhaps play from another suit over hearts, securing one win

indicators.note: in a down clue this piece sits above the next one
holding inside, so the letter for one is put within the card term

parts.note: to trump at cards is to play from the trump suit rather than follow suit
I is the Roman numeral for one
H is the abbreviation for hearts in bridge

explanation.surface: A card player wins by playing a different suit over hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' puts I into TRUMP, and 'over' sets that above H in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great victory or win.

clue.text: Policeman in charge in bid for acceptance

indicators.note: placed within, so the abbreviation sits inside the word for a bid

parts.note: an offer is a bid made in hope of acceptance
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge, read here with the word in just before it

explanation.surface: A senior police chief makes a bid hoping it will be accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words 'in' sit side by side: the first is part of the abbreviation IC, and only the second signals the container, so a solver should not treat 'in charge' as an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer is a policeman, a general term for a member of the force.

clue.text: Somewhere in church match shortly is concluded with lines?

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter of the word for match is dropped

parts.note: a vesta is a short wooden match
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines a train runs on

explanation.surface: A cricket or football match ends early in a parish setting with lines to recite.
explanation.walkthrough: A VESTA is an old-fashioned name for a match, not a sporting fixture; 'shortly' trims it to VEST, and RY is railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is a room in a church where clergy robe and vestments are kept.

clue.text: What will have character shortly immersed in haze?

definitions.text: What will have character shortly immersed in haze?

indicators.note: sunk inside, so the trimmed word goes within the word for haze

parts.note: smog is a polluted haze in the air

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: kind means character or nature, as in 'things of that kind'

explanation.surface: A riddle about where a person might end up wrapped in a cloud of fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims KIND, and 'immersed in' signals the container. The whole clue doubles as a description of a smoking area, where people sit in the haze, which is why it reads as one riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoking area or carriage is where anyone present sits surrounded by a cloud of tobacco fumes.

clue.text: Good-natured? A fine story

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a fable is a short moral tale

explanation.surface: A question about someone's temperament, answered with a pleasant little tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An affable person is friendly and easy-going, a synonym for good-natured.

clue.text: This is strong meat

parts.note: the word means both physical strength or muscle and a jellied meat made from a pig's head

explanation.walkthrough: One word means muscle power and is also a cold pressed meat from pork, hence 'strong meat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscular strength and a jellied pork dish share the one word, so it is literally strong meat.

clue.text: Cleaner's put marks on small ornament

parts.note: a char is a British term for a cleaning lady
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: The cleaning lady leaves marks on a little decorative piece.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is an old British word for a cleaner. M follows CHAR, as 'put marks on' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm is a small trinket worn on a bracelet, so it is a little ornament.

clue.text: Cutting fish without right article takes time

indicators.note: outside, so the fish surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fishmonger cuts up a fish without the right tool and takes ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here is the old sense 'outside', so the fish surrounds R to give TRENCH, not the modern sense of lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A trenchant remark is incisive and sharp, so cutting in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Ultimately right to be agitated when son's gone missing as a small child will do

definitions.text: as a small child will do

indicators.note: the letter for son leaves and something takes its place

parts.note: to seethe is to be inwardly agitated or furious
S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is upset at their son's disappearance, behaving like a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: SEETHE loses its S ('son's gone missing') and T, the last letter of 'right' ('Ultimately'), goes in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies and toddlers teethe as their first milk teeth come through, so it is what a small child does.

clue.text: With complete year's guarantee

parts.note: arrant means complete or utter, as in arrant nonsense
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A product comes with a full year's guarantee.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranty is a written guarantee covering repair or replacement of goods.
